analysis.title: Europe Open - Putting AI to the test
key_insights: Tech selloff deepened overnight ahead of Nvidia earnings after the US cash close (~21:30 GMT). Kospi was the worst performer at -2.5%. Nasdaq futures were flat at print, so US futures downside momentum is more modest than in Asia.
Asia desk says internet and AI stocks fell on concern that a new curb damages future AI training ability: Alibaba -4.94%, Z.AI -3.5%, Minimax -2.72%.
WSJ reports Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, despite calls from some investors and employees for his return.
USTs rose slightly overnight on risk-off sentiment and AI pessimism. Duration stayed in a tight range, flows were light, and volume rebounded to about 0.8x recent averages.

RBA minutes: the majority voted against a hike on concern the economy is near a sharp downturn. Members who favored a hike said inflation risks were skewed to the upside. February carries the highest hike weight in OIS at 7bp, and near-term hike odds remain limited.

Hedge funds returned to USD buying last week with strong net inflows versus G10 and EM currencies. The Citi positioning indicator (CFPI) for the dollar is +2.5 for leveraged and +2.0 for investors overall, out of a maximum of +10. Citi's quant framework is bearish USD given recent gains and long positioning.

FX session was quiet, with interbank volumes 24% below the 30-day average. Implied vols stayed sidelined, and short-term realized vols have not outperformed the higher implied base. The options desk favors owning AUD downside vol, with 3m 25d RR at 1.35v AUD put.

USS Theodore arrived in the Persian Gulf, the third US carrier in the Middle East per Centcom. This gives the US administration more options if it chooses to re-escalate strikes on Iran. Brent was at $91.87, slightly lower.
Trump attends the ASEAN summit today and then the APEC summit, where a trilateral with Putin and Xi on Thursday is the highlight. Iran is an expected topic and Ukraine is not, per reports.

UK October labor data at print showed a lower unemployment rate and strong wages. A wage surprise would strengthen the case for a December BoE hike, though Wednesday's inflation print matters more. Citi economists expected wages to moderate to 3.6% 3m/YoY.

Ahead: US October retail sales (13:30 GMT) are expected at +0.2% MoM vs +0.8% prior, core ex-auto and gas +0.3%, control group +0.4%. Fed speakers are Musalem, Waller, Hammack and Williams. German ZEW is due at 10:00 GMT and the Hungary rate decision is expected to be a hold at 5.5%.
